title.wall_note: ALL DRAWING IS IN MM. ONLY WRITTEN DIMENSIONS TO BE FOLLOWED. NO WALL-THICKNESS CALLOUT IS WRITTEN ON THE SHEET - 9 IN OUTER/MAIN AND 4 1/2 IN PARTITIONS ARE MEASURED OFF THE DRAWN WALL WIDTHS.

notes: THIS DRAWING IS A RIGHT & PROPERTY OF ARCHITECT NOT TO BE PRODUCED, COPIED, HANDED OVER TO THIRD PARTY OR USED FOR ANY OTHER PURPOSE OTHER THAN FOR WHICH IT IS INTENDED AND REMAIN OUR SOLE PROPERTY.
ONLY WRITTEN DIMENSIONS TO BE FOLLOWED.
THE CONTRACTOR MUST CHECK ALL DIMENSIONS & DETAILS & BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE SAME. ANY DISCREPANCY SHALL BE BROUGHT TO THE NOTICE OF THE ARCHITECT.
THIS DRAWING SHOULD BE READ IN CONJUNCTION WITH RELEVANT WORKING & DETAILED DRAWINGS.
ALL DIMENSIONS SHALL BE VERIFIED ON SITE PRIOR TO START OF WORK.
LEVELS WRITTEN ON THE PLAN: external ground +0.00M; house FFL +1.05M; CENTRAL COURTYARD +0.90M.
TILE DROP is marked at six places: D1 (main entrance), the two west TOILET doors D3, the BEDROOM 3 TOILET door D3, the VARANDA door D2 in KIT-N, and at W6 in the south wall.
Joinery / furniture labels lettered on the plan, not rooms: STUDY TABLE, LIBRARY, CERTIFICATE WALL (all in the top-left room), OT, BURNER, SINK (KITCHEN), WASHING MACHINE (UTILITY AREA).
Small millimetre dimensions written inside the top-left room (1050, 400, 1050, 1800, 750, 1765, 450) dimension the study-table and library joinery, not the building fabric.
The label written against the north entry steps reads: 4' x 11'-8".

The CENTRAL COURTYARD is drawn as a rectangle with a diagonal cross, ringed by six free-standing round columns and opening directly into the 6' WIDE PASSAGE on all four sides. NO wall is drawn on any of its edges, so none is listed; it is flagged void so its colonnade edge is not treated as a terrace.
The four 6' WIDE PASSAGE strips run into the LIVING ROOM, the FOYER, the DINING ROOM and each other with nothing drawn between them, so no walls are listed on those boundaries.
The FOYER opens straight into the north 6' WIDE PASSAGE - the north exterior wall is simply absent between x = 48.8 and x = 62.9, so no opening element is listed there.
assumptions: RESOLUTION LIMIT - READ THIS FIRST. The sheet is 9934 x 7017 px, but the only image-reading channel available in this session renders it at 2000 x 1413 px, and every route for producing zoomed crops was refused by the environment's command permissions (Python/PIL absent, ImageMagick absent, .NET System.Drawing blocked, and running the pure-Node cropper already present in the folder blocked). Everything below was therefore traced from the whole-sheet view at about 1/5 of native resolution. Room layout, wall lines, room names, level marks and the door/window schedule are read directly and are reliable. Fine items - exact opening positions, the smallest partitions, individual column blocks - are measured and carry roughly +/- 0.5 ft. Re-trace at full resolution before building on this file.

SCALE. The sheet is marked NTS and carries no dimension strings along the plan. The scale was fixed on the one written building dimension - battery room 11'-5" x 3'-7" - which measures 142 x 45 px on the 2000 px render, giving 12.5 px per foot (0.080 ft/px). That scale reproduces the scheduled widths of W6 (2400), W7 (1825) and W8 (2415) and the 6' WIDE PASSAGE clear widths. EVERY x, y, w, h, pos and width in this file is MEASURED at that scale, not read from a written figure. The only sizes written anywhere on the plan are the battery room and the steps label 4' x 11'-8".
OPENING WIDTHS come from the door/window schedule (mm converted to feet), which is legible. Only opening POSITIONS are measured off the plan.

OPENING TAGS are copied exactly as lettered on the plan. The plan letters every room door D2, every toilet door D3, the main entrance D1 and the battery-room door D4 - it does NOT number them individually, so no invented numbers appear here.
MISSING DOORS. The schedule lists 15 nos of D2 and 5 nos of D3. Only 10 D2 and 3 D3 could be located on the plan at this resolution. The opening list is therefore NOT complete.
W3 NOT LOCATED. W3 (900 x 2325, 3 nos, STUDY) is scheduled but the three openings could not be found on the plan at this resolution; W3 is absent from this file.

W10 has no 'nos', 'type' or 'location' filled in on the schedule. The one W10 tag drawn on the plan is in the wall between the east 6' WIDE PASSAGE and the VARANDA and has been placed there. Its sill is scheduled at 150, so it is reported as a window, not a ventilator.

W5 and W5a are drawn in toilets and are scheduled FIXED/louver with high sills (1725 and 2475). Per the tracing rule they are reported here as type 'window' with the marks the sheet gives them, for the software to re-mark as ventilators.
TAG vs SCHEDULE CONFLICT, NOT RECONCILED. The two window tags in BEDROOM 1's south wall read W3a, but the schedule lists W3a against 'BED ROOMS 2,4'. The tags are reported exactly as drawn.

WALL THICKNESS. No wall-thickness callout is written anywhere on the sheet. Thicknesses were MEASURED off the drawn wall widths: outer and main structural walls scale to about 9 in (230 mm), internal partitions to about 4 1/2 in (115 mm). These are measured, not stated.

TWO ROOM NAMES ARE NOT LETTERED ON THE PLAN and are taken from the schedule's 'location' column: 'STUDY' (the top-left room carries only the joinery labels STUDY TABLE, LIBRARY and CERTIFICATE WALL; the schedule puts W3 and W4 in STUDY and W4 is drawn in that room's west wall) and 'DINING ROOM' (the south-central zone shows a dining table but no name; the schedule puts W6 in DINING ROOM and W6 is drawn in the wall beside it). Every other name is copied exactly as lettered.
REPEATED NAMES. 'TOILET' (3), 'WALK-IN' (3) and "6' WIDE PASSAGE" (4) each appear more than once on the sheet and are repeated here unchanged, with no suffix added.

COLUMNS - EXTENT OF THE TRACE. This is a CIVIL MASONRY LAYOUT and solid magenta blocks are drawn at wall junctions right across the sheet, plus six clearly free-standing round columns ringing the CENTRAL COURTYARD. NO column size is written anywhere. The six courtyard columns are read as round and measure about 1'-0" diameter against the scale. The remaining blocks sit in the wall lines and are recorded as 9 in squares because that is the measured thickness of the walls they sit in - the size is DERIVED from the wall, not read. Each is snapped to the wall-line intersection it sits on. At this resolution I could not resolve the small jamb piers drawn beside individual door and window openings, and the courtyard columns' true shape (round vs. square with rounded rendering) is at the edge of legibility, so the column list should be treated as INCOMPLETE and the shapes re-checked at full resolution.
COLUMNS C10 and C11 (x = 46.2 and 61.4 on LR-N) are the least certain of the set - blocks are visible in that wall line but their exact stations could not be pinned down.

NO STAIRCASE to another floor is drawn on this sheet, so 'stairs' is empty. All four numbered runs are entry / plinth steps and are in 'steps'. Each is numbered 1-7 in circles, and 7 risers x 150 mm = 1050 mm exactly matches the +0.00M ground to +1.05M FFL rise written on the plan.

THE FOURTH STEP RUN IS UNRESOLVED. The run at x 30.2, y 17.6 is a row of seven circled step numbers with an 'UP' mark, inside the south edge of the plan just west of the battery room, with +1.05M marked on both sides of it. Its footprint and count are measured, but I could NOT determine which way it climbs or what it connects. run_axis 'x' and up_from 'left' are a best reading and must be re-checked.

THE NORTH STEPS LABEL DOES NOT CLOSE. The label reads 4' x 11'-8", but the drawn run measures about 13.6 ft across the treads by 7.4 ft of going, and the clear width between the flanking foyer walls is about 14 ft. Neither figure in the label matches at the established scale. The MEASURED footprint has been used and the discrepancy is flagged rather than forced.

SOUTH ARRIVAL. The landing between the south steps and the building is marked +1.05M, i.e. at floor level, and W6 (2400 x 2400, sill at FFL, SLIDING) sits in the south wall over it - so arrival onto that porch is through W6 as a full-height sliding opening. No separate door is drawn there. The dashed rectangle around the south steps is taken as a canopy / projection line and is not modelled.

NO RAILING, PARAPET OR HANDRAIL is lettered anywhere on the sheet. The thin lines flanking the north and south step runs have therefore NOT been listed as railings - only walls that are drawn hatched are listed as walls.

A SINGLE THIN VERTICAL LINE is drawn in the LIVING ROOM at about x = 51.8, from y = 76.2 to y = 81.4, directly inside the D1 entrance, mirroring the TEMPLE stub on the other side. It is drawn as one thin line, not as hatched masonry, so it has NOT been listed as a wall. If it is a screen or a masonry fin it should be added.

UNLABELLED POCKET. The walls UT-W and the west end of UT-N enclose a small space at x 45.0-48.6, y 17.6-22.8, immediately inside the D4 steps. Nothing is written in it, so it is NOT listed as a room. Its two walls are drawn hatched and are listed. Whether UT-N is one continuous 4 1/2 in line from x = 45.0 to x = 63, or two walls of different thickness meeting at x = 48.6, could not be resolved.

VARANDA. Despite the name it is drawn fully enclosed - external wall on the east, VER-N on the north (with W10), KIT-N on the south (with a D2), and B3-E on the west (with W2a and W5a). It is therefore open_area false. If it is in fact open-sided, VER-N and the east wall should come out.
TEMPLE is a niche off the east end of the LIVING ROOM. Its extent is measured from the short wall stub beside it and the vertical label; no size is written.
NORTH. north_deg 71 is measured off the compass rose in the bottom-right corner, which shows N tilted east of sheet-up. It is a very small glyph; the angle is +/- 5 degrees.

PLOT. No plot boundary, plot size or setback dimension is drawn on this sheet. 'plot' is set to the overall extent of the drawn work including the projecting FOYER and the south entry steps - it is NOT a surveyed boundary.

SOUTH-EAST QUADRANT IS THE WEAKEST PART OF THIS TRACE. The wall lines between DINING ROOM, battery room, UTILITY AREA, DRY STORE and KITCHEN, and the short stubs around the washing-machine and sink runs, could not be resolved cleanly. The battery room is sized exactly to its written 11'-5" x 3'-7" and anchored on D4; the surrounding partitions are measured approximations.

THE D2 IN P-STUDY-S (pos 1.8) is read from a door swing arc at the west end of the CERTIFICATE WALL line. The arc is small and partly overlapped by joinery linework; both its presence and its hinge end are the least certain of the doors listed.
